newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Nov 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Nov 22.

text.p: Toyota said it plans to cut back its export volumes rather than risk political consequences, the Wall Street Journal reported.
- CompuServe Corp reported a record quarterly loss, set plans to retreat from the consumer market and shut down a family service it launched less than a year ago.
- American Airlines of AMR Corp will buy its jets exclusively from Boeing Co for the next two decades.
- Coca-Cola Enterprises Inc's proposed $1.85 billion purchase of a British bottler is being reviewed by regulators amid protests from rivals.
- Jobless claims surged by 17,000 last week to 344,000, the highest level in four months.
- U.S. regulators are weighing possible action against Asahi Bank Ltd for allegedly hindering a probe of its New York operations.
- Tele-Communications Inc said it plans to raise cable rates and add new channels next year.
- Lawyers for a former Texaco Inc official charged with obstruction of justice plan to argue that prosecutors are pushing criminal law beyond its intent.
- Gold futures dropped to 19-month lows as Switzerland began considering abolishing its central bank's gold requirement.
- Russia entered international debt markets for the first time since 1917 with a $1-billion Eurobond issue.
- Ronald Perelman's representatives warned Marvel Entertainment Group Inc bondholders that Marvel would be forced to file for bankruptcy protection unless they approved a reorganization plan.
- The Securities and Exchange Commission accused Montedison SpA of falsely writing off hundreds of millions of dollars in bribes as a bad loan.
- Short interest rose 8.9 percent on the New York Stock Exchange in the latest month, setting another record.
- Sunglass Hut International Inc posted a wider-than-expected quarterly loss and disclosed plans to close up to 100 retail outlets.
- As the insurance brokerage business soured in recent years, industry leader Marsh & McLennan has been prompted up by its fast-growing mutual fund subsidiary, Putnam Investments.
